frank: quick AH follow-up - finance question about classifying reserved capacity vs hardware leases. If infra signs a 24-month Dedicated GPU lease, is that CapEx or Opex for runway modeling?

maria (CFO): Short answer: runway modeling treats cash outflows as they occur. Accounting classification (CapEx vs Opex) follows GAAP: if it's effectively buying a capital asset or a lease that meets capitalization thresholds, Accounting will capitalize and amortize. For runway we still show the cash outflow timing (i.e., up-front payments hit runway immediately).

lucy (Accounting): To add: for a 24-month lease that gives Redwood control of the hardware and meets the lease capitalization criteria, we capitalize on the balance sheet and amortize. But the cash payment schedule still reduces bank balance when paid. Please provide the contract terms and payment schedule in the intake.

frank: Got it. For a vendor that offers 12mo prepay vs monthly billing at higher unit cost, which should teams prefer from runway POV?

maria (CFO): From pure runway perspective, monthly billing is easier (smoothed out). Prepay can give unit-cost savings but takes cash up front. If prepay materially reduces cost per token and payback is < 12 months, Procurement+Finance Ops may approve after reviewing FIN-300. Include cash-flow pro forma.

rachel (Legal): One nuance: prepaid contracts sometimes have limited exit/credit terms. Procurement will try to get refunds/credits or SLA-based credits. Legal should review long-term prepay terms > $25k.

dylan (Finance Ops): For decision speed: if the prepay is < $15k and ROI > 20% within 6 months, tag it "ops-fast-track" in FIN-300 and we aim for 48hr turnaround. If > $15k, standard intake applies. Template: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/FIN-300

frank: If we sign a 24-month commit but later need to scale down, will we be stuck paying for idle capacity?

maria (CFO): That's why Procurement negotiates flex clauses. Standard asks: 30-day scale notice; partial-credit for unused baseline; and SLA service credits. Flag variability in the intake and Procurement will negotiate.

sam (CEO): Strategic note: we want predictable unit economics but flexibility. If a commit materially reduces cost and lets product ship faster, weigh the runway hit vs long-term savings. Finance will lean toward deals that improve 12mo economics.

frank: Who signs for capital leases vs operational contracts? Manager level vs exec?

lucy (Accounting): Capital leases that create material balance sheet impact (> $100k PV) go to CFO for approval. Operational contracts follow Procurement flow. For commitments with annualized >= $50k, Exec sign-off still required.

dylan (Finance Ops): Quick approval flow we use: Requester -> Manager (budget check) -> Finance Ops (policy) -> Procurement -> Legal if > $25k or touches data -> CFO/Exec if >= $50k annualized or balance sheet impact > $100k.

procure-bot: Created FIN-300-42: "24mo Dedicated lease inquiry - infra" and assigned to dylan.

frank: Thanks. Action items: infra to attach payment schedule + utilization forecast to FIN-300; Procurement to push for flex clauses; Legal to review if > $25k.

maria (CFO): And teams: include a simple two-scenario table (base vs stress) in the form so FP&A can show runway impact quickly. We'll post a short decision guide in the docs page by EOD.

sam (CEO): Thanks all 44d. Keep Finance in the loop early on any multi-month commitments.
